clue.text: A record an accountant had of the beast

parts.note: LP is a long-playing record
ACA stands for Associate of the Institute of Chartered Accountants

explanation.surface: A bookkeeper's ledger lists an entry about some animal he owned.
explanation.walkthrough: LP is a long-playing vinyl record; ACA is a British accountancy qualification. 'had of the' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The alpaca is a South American grazing animal related to the llama, so it is a kind of beast.

clue.text: I am producing expression of impatience, being full of mischief

parts.note: contracted, I am becomes I'm
pish is an old exclamation of contempt or impatience

explanation.surface: Someone tutting with irritation is shown as a little troublemaker.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone playful and naughty like a little sprite is described this way.

clue.text: Beastly attractiveness?

parts.note: read literally, the allure a creature exerts; really an old name for hypnotism or raw personal charm

explanation.surface: A wry remark on the appeal of brutes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beastly' usually means nasty, but here it means belonging to an animal, pointing to the phrase for physical charisma (and Mesmer's hypnotic theory).
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names strong personal or sexual charisma, here taken as the pull exerted by a creature.

clue.text: They drop the bricklayer's tool, not trowel initially, first used in carpentry

indicators.note: first says the reduced tool name stands at the front, ahead of the other piece
'not' tells us a letter is to be left out of the tool's name

parts.note: a jointer is a bricklayer's tool for finishing mortar joints

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word trowel
'They drop the' means the word They loses the three letters spelling the

explanation.surface: Builders put down their trowels before starting some woodwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drop' takes THE from THEY, leaving Y; 'not trowel initially' removes T from JOINTER, giving JOINER, which comes 'first'. 'used in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Joinery is the craft of making wooden fittings such as doors and window frames, a branch of woodworking.

clue.text: Clergyman's parish?

parts.note: a vicar's benefice is called a living, so his patch is jokingly the realm of that living; the phrase really means the world of those still alive

explanation.surface: A question about where a vicar works.
explanation.walkthrough: In the Church of England a 'living' is a clergyman's paid post with its parish.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means being alive and among people, punningly read as the territory of a church benefice.

clue.text: Cause of deflation en route

parts.note: deflation suggests economics, but here it is a tyre losing air while you are driving

explanation.surface: An economist's phrase about what brings prices down along the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Deflation' tempts towards finance; it is literal, air escaping from a tyre.
explanation.definitionFit: A hole in a tyre lets the air out, so it flattens a wheel during a journey.

clue.text: Hard grains Maureen found in saline concoction

indicators.note: found in says one piece sits inside the other
a concoction is a mixture, so the letters of saline are mixed up

parts.note: Mo is a short form of the name Maureen

explanation.surface: A woman named Maureen turns up in a salty brew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concoction' rearranges SALINE to SELINA, and 'found in' puts MO inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Semolina is the coarse hard particles of durum wheat milled for pasta and puddings.

clue.text: Corporal ignited gas before dance

indicators.note: before puts the flame ahead of the corporal

parts.note: burning gas gives a flame
a corporal is an NCO, a non-commissioned officer

explanation.surface: A soldier lights the gas before taking to the dance floor.
explanation.definitionFit: Flamenco is the passionate Andalusian style of music and footwork.

clue.text: Aga left Guatemala replacement charm

indicators.note: replacement says the remaining letters are put back in a new order

explanation.surface: A cooking range left behind in Central America is swapped for a lucky trinket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Aga left' takes A, G, A out of GUATEMALA, and 'replacement' rearranges the remaining U, T, E, M, L, A. An Aga is a British brand of cast-iron cooker.
explanation.definitionFit: An amulet is a small object worn as a protective charm against evil.

clue.text: Nothing in available charge

indicators.note: in tells us the zero sits inside the other piece

parts.note: something in, as in stock, is available
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: No cash is available to cover a fee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'charge' looks like a fee; it is electrical, an ion being a charged particle.
explanation.definitionFit: An ion is an atom or molecule carrying an electrical charge, so it can be called a charged particle.

clue.text: Novel Scottish trinket

explanation.surface: A new Scots ornament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel Scottish' reads as 'new from Scotland', but it is a novel by (Walter) Scott, 'The Talisman' (1825).
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Walter Scott wrote the crusader novel of this title, and the word also means a lucky charm or keepsake.

clue.text: His job is to prevent ill-feeling

definitions.text: His job is to prevent ill-feeling

parts.words: His job is to prevent ill-feeling
parts.note: ill-feeling reads as resentment, but literally it means feeling sick, which a medic works to stop

explanation.surface: A peacemaker who keeps people from bearing grudges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ill-feeling' seems to mean animosity; read literally it is sickness.
explanation.definitionFit: A physician's work is keeping patients healthy, preventing illness.

clue.text: Notedly eligible fellow?

parts.note: an eligible fellow is an unmarried man, and notedly hints at musical notes, giving a degree in that subject

explanation.surface: A famously available single man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notedly' seems to mean 'notably'; it means 'in terms of notes', pointing to a music degree.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a university degree in music, with the title read as an unattached man.

clue.text: Character giving honour to Italian leader

parts.note: CH is Companion of Honour, a British award

indicators.note: leader means the opening letter of the word Italian

explanation.surface: An Italian chief is decorated with an award.
explanation.definitionFit: Chi is a letter of the Greek alphabet, and letters are characters.

clue.text: Green approach not particularly close

explanation.surface: An eco-friendly policy that falls short of hitting the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Green' is a golf green; the closely mown run of a golf hole leads to it. A 'fair way' off is some distance away.
explanation.definitionFit: On a golf course the mown strip leads up to the putting surface, and a fair way off means rather distant.

clue.text: Rabble-rouser with awkward gait brought up roster

indicators.note: awkward signals the letters of gait are arranged clumsily
in a down clue brought up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: a rota is a roster of duties

explanation.surface: A troublemaker with an ungainly walk has the duty list brought forward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'awkward' rearranges GAIT as AGIT; 'brought up' turns ROTA into ATOR.
explanation.definitionFit: An agitator stirs up crowds to protest, the classic troublemaker.

clue.text: Moving free not, say, from this

definitions.text: Moving free not, say, from this

parts.words: Moving free not, say, from this
parts.note: shifting the letters of this knot gives something that sounds like free not, a reverse anagram with a sound-alike

explanation.surface: Advice on how to get loose.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearranging REEF KNOT gives FREE KNOT, which 'say' tells you to hear as 'free not'.
explanation.definitionFit: This sailor's square knot of two half-hitches is the source whose rearranged letters yield the clue's phrase.

clue.text: Each with the remarkably swift feline

indicators.note: remarkably suggests the letters of each and the are oddly arranged

explanation.surface: Every one of these cats is astonishingly fast.
explanation.definitionFit: The cheetah is a big cat famed as the fastest land animal.

clue.text: Pull from the east?

explanation.surface: A tug coming out of the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: Going from the east you head 'to W', west.
explanation.definitionFit: To tow is to drag a vehicle behind you, and setting off from the east means heading to the west, written as the compass letter.

clue.text: Indirectly as a neck is turned

indicators.note: is turned signals the letters of as a neck are rearranged

explanation.surface: Glancing sideways as one twists one's head.
explanation.definitionFit: Looking askance means glancing sideways or obliquely, often with suspicion.

clue.text: Make personal donation reveal one's true character

explanation.surface: Someone gives generously and thereby shows who they really are.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally the phrase is handing over yourself as a gift, and idiomatically it means betraying your true nature.

clue.text: From Canadians we received return in kind

indicators.note: From signals the letters are taken out of the run Canadians we received

explanation.surface: We got a reply in kind from people in Canada.
explanation.definitionFit: To answer is to respond, giving back a reply of the same sort.

clue.text: One over-familiar once more

parts.note: one is the article a
fresh can mean cheeky or too forward

explanation.surface: A cheeky person tries it again.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something afresh means starting again, anew.

clue.text: Ship can be tied up?

explanation.surface: A boat may be moored.
explanation.walkthrough: A packet (boat) carried mail; a packet is also a parcel, something wrapped and tied with string.
explanation.definitionFit: A packet boat was a ship carrying post, and a small parcel is wrapped and bound with string.

clue.text: Making recommendations during days Ivor rebelled

indicators.note: rebelled suggests the letters of days and Ivor rise up into a new order

explanation.surface: Ivor revolted at a time when he was giving counsel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'during' is a link word, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An advisory body gives counsel or suggestions without power to enforce them.

clue.text: One article from man north of the border

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
an is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A single item from a Scotsman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'North of the border' means Scotland seen from England; Ian is the Scottish form of John.
explanation.definitionFit: Ian is a typically Scottish given name, so a Scot might well bear it.

clue.text: Endlessly stir up river first, it's leaky

indicators.note: first puts the river at the front

parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

indicators.note: endlessly means the last letter of the stirring word is cut off

parts.note: to rouse is to stir up

explanation.surface: Constantly agitating the waters, the river leaks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Endlessly' removes the final E of ROUSE. 'it's' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Something porous lets liquid seep through its tiny holes, as a sponge or unglazed pot does.

clue.text: Make little of it

parts.note: make little of usually means belittle, but here it means reduce something in size or length

explanation.surface: Dismiss something as unimportant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make little of' normally means 'disparage'; read literally, it means shrink or abridge.
explanation.definitionFit: To condense is to shorten or compress, making a text or substance smaller.
